1/ JSEF v1.3.0 is out. JSEF = a Spring Boot 3.x Java security-teaching framework AND a benchmark for measuring how well SAST tools and LLMs hunt vulnerabilities. Today: we hardened the "hard tasks" part. 🧵

2/ Why "hard tasks"? Most vuln benchmarks are single-shot: "here's code, is it vulnerable?" JSEF v1.3.0 adds long-horizon samples that require multi-step tracing, tool use, and planning — e.g. reconstruct a CommonsCollections gadget  chain or trace a cross-file fastjson autotype

3/ What's new (56 samples, +40 trace nodes):
  • Long-horizon LT (16): cross-file / state-machine / gadget-chain / concat / version-gated
  • Code-quality & perf-DoS PERF (15): slow SQL, leaks, lock-held sleep, ReDoS
  • LGTM/CodeQL gap coverage (14): trust-boundary,

4/ Every sample is dual-sourced: a // [CHECKPOINT] annotation at the exact sink line + a row in expectedresults.csv. validate_checkpoints.py exits 0 — 439 ids consistent, 0 invalid trace nodes. No real exploit code; localhost-demo only.

5/ Goal: measure LLM planning ability & consistency on complex vuln analysis (not just yes/no). Try it, compare models, file issues.
